name: human-handoff
title: Human Handoff
description: When a person takes over from the agent, and what they're handed. Takes a `stage` (`agentHandling`, `waitingForPerson`, `personHandling`, `returnedToAgent`), the agent's `reason` for stepping back in its own words, a `context` list of the facts a person would otherwise have to ask for again, the `person` who has it now, a `waitingFor` duration, and `onTakeOver` / `onReturnToAgent`. The context is the component, not the button: handoffs usually lose everything, so the customer repeats themselves and whoever takes over re-reads a transcript to find three facts. Listing what the agent already tried is part of that, since offering a customer the same rejected remedy twice is the most common way a handoff goes wrong. It also works in both directions, because handing a finished job back to the agent is the half products forget. Purely presentational. Use it in support, operations and any agent that can reach the end of what it may decide. Not for a single approval (that is AI Approval Gate), and not for a question the agent could answer itself (that is Agent Ask).
docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Fill `context` with the facts a colleague would ask for in the first thirty seconds, including what the agent already tried.

meta.engineeringNotes: Stage is a four-value enum rather than a boolean because the return leg is a real state with its own copy, and products that model handoff as 'escalated: true' have nowhere to put the moment a person finishes and the agent resumes. Waiting is styled in the waiting colour with full stillness, the same treatment approvals get, so a queue of handoffs reads at a glance without a separate legend. The context list is `dl` markup rather than free text so a caller can render five facts consistently and a screen reader hears label-and-value pairs, and it sits inside the component rather than being left to a slot because the whole failure mode is teams shipping a handoff button with no payload.
meta.motionNotes: Nothing animates, in any stage. A waiting handoff is a person's turn and the strongest signal available is complete stillness; a pulsing 'needs attention' badge here would compete with the queue around it and train people to ignore it.
